question: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$. Without explicitly calculating $A^{-1}$, determine whether $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$ or $(AB)^{-1} = A^{-1}B^{-1}$, justifying your answer using matrix properties.

options.A: $(AB)^{-1}=B^{-1}A^{-1}$ because the order reverses when taking the inverse of a product
options.B: $(AB)^{-1}=A^{-1}B^{-1}$ because inverse does not change the order
